title: SMB flat+credits rough math
body:
Context:
- Goal: quick sketch of a "flat+credits" starter plan for SMBs that is simple for GTM, predictable for customers, and lets us preserve unit economics via overage pricing + optional priority lanes.
- Want something between pure PAYG and metered bands: lower cognitive load, easy to compare, but scales with usage.

Assumptions (rough):
- Infra marginal cost (hosted inference average, blended across models we expect SMBs to use): ~ $0.0009 per token generated (includes GPU amortization, network, infra ops).
- Avg tokens per request: 120 tokens (prompt + response) for typical SMB chat/assist flows.
- Embeddings: treat separately, avg embed request = 1536-dim single vector; cost ~ $0.02 per embedding (in infra terms).
- Priority routing (lower latency SLO): ~2x infra cost impact because of lower batching and reserved capacity.
- Target gross margin for hosted plan: 70%+ (we want room for S&M/support).

"Flat+credits" sketch (three starter tiers):
1) Starter: $29 / month flat + 0. No included credits, low support. Overage: $0.012 per 1k tokens.
2) Growth: $199 / month flat + 200k token credits included. Overage: $0.009 per 1k tokens. Priority lane add-on: +$100/mo for 1ms-3ms P50 improvement (for small peak).
3) Scale-SMB: $499 / month flat + 1M token credits included. Overage: $0.007 per 1k tokens. Includes limited embedding bundle: 1k embeddings/mo.

Why these numbers? back-of-envelope unit math:
- Convert infra per-token to per-1k: $0.0009/token => $0.9 per 1k tokens (that seems high). Wait — sanity check: this is wrong: I meant $0.0009 per token => $0.9 per 1k tokens, which is too high relative to market. Let's correct base infra guess to $0.00009/token => $0.09 per 1k tokens. (Keep note: clarify model mix later.)
- Using $0.00009/token: per-1k token infra cost = $0.09. To hit 70% gross margin, list price per-1k should be about $0.30 (0.09 / (1 - 0.7) = 0.3). That maps to $0.30 per 1k tokens.
- Our proposed overage rates above (~$0.007-$0.012 per 1k) are MUCH lower — they were modeled on previous internal numbers for quantized on-prem costs. Reconcile: we need consistent baseline.

Reset with better calibrated assumptions (targeting hosted mixed models - small Llama-like variants + caching):
- blended infra cost per token (amortized + ops): $0.00002/token => $0.02 per 1k tokens (aggressive, assumes heavy prefix caching and small models).
- reasonable retail overage target to keep 70% margin: price_per_1k = cost / (1 - margin) => 0.02 / 0.3 = $0.066 => ~$0.07 per 1k tokens.
- So overage bands should be in the $0.05-$0.10 per 1k token range depending on tier.

Apply to tiers (revised):
- Starter ($29): Overage $0.10 per 1k; includes 0 credits. Break-even usage to pay for plan: 29 / 0.10 * 1k tokens = 290k tokens equivalent. That gives a perceived value to customers who use >290k tokens/mo. For light users it's a seat-like feel.
- Growth ($199): includes 200k tokens. Equivalent overage avoided value at $0.08/1k = 200k * 0.08 / 1000 = $16. So the customer pays $183 effectively for usage-free bucket. Unit economics: cost to us for those 200k tokens = 200k/1k * $0.02 = $4. So gross margin on included credits is excellent.
- Scale-SMB ($499): includes 1M tokens. Cost to us = 1k * $0.02 * 1000 = wait wrong units. Simpler: 1M tokens * $0.00002 = $20 infra cost. If we price the plan at $499, margin on included tokens alone is very high (should subsidize support).

Priority lane add-on math:
- If reserved capacity halves batching efficiency, infra cost multiplier ~2x. For 1M tokens, extra infra cost = delta = (2x - 1x) * cost = $20 extra for 1M tokens if base cost = $20 => very small. So offering a $100/mo priority add-on has high margin. But need to ensure real world latency tests.

Credit consumption examples (for sales):
- Short Q&A bot: avg 40 tokens/turn, 10 turns/day for 22 days = 8,800 tokens/mo. Fits in Starter easily.
- Helpdesk assist (multi-turn): avg 400 tokens/session * 200 sessions/mo = 80k tokens/mo => Growth tier with included 200k is safe.
- Content generation heavy: 2k tokens/article * 100 articles/mo = 200k tokens/mo => Growth tier borderline, Scale-SMB recommended.

Edge cases and considerations:
- Embeddings: priced separately (e.g., $0.02 per embedding as a base) or as a bundle in Scale-SMB. SMBs with heavy search vector usage will exceed token assumptions and should be steered to dedicated pricing.
- Caching / credits expiration: include a 90-day roll-over for unused credits to simplify sales objections? Might complicate accounting.
- Nanobatch behaviour: encourage caching to reduce cost; provide a dashboard showing token/unit savings from caching so customers can self-optimize.

Open questions / todo:
- Re-run infra blended cost calc using actual model mix (gpt-4x-small-ish? redwood verified models) -> need input from applied-ml (Evan) on expected model mix for SMB signal.
- Decide whether to denominate credits in tokens or 'requests'. Tokens are transparent but confusing for product folks. Could expose both (X credits = Y tokens typical).
- Confirm embedding cost with infra team; current $0.02 is a placeholder.
- Create sample sales one-pager that shows three use cases mapping to tiers + cost math.

Quick recommendation:
- Ship a MVR (minimum viable retainer) flat+credits offering: Starter $29 (no credits, high overage), Growth $199 (200k credits, $0.08/1k overage), Scale-SMB $499 (1M credits + 1k embeddings, $0.06/1k overage). Launch as "preview" with opt-in priority add-on $100/mo.

Notes to self:
- Keep numbers intentionally conservative on infra cost when talking to finance.
- Build a short eval script to estimate monthly token consumption from product telemetry (histogram of tokens per request, percentiles).
- Put a banner in the console for SMB customers: "See estimated monthly cost" with flat-plan suggestion based on current 30-day usage.
